sources.text:
Mælifell (Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈmaiːlɪˌfɛtl̥] ) is a volcano located in Southern Iceland.
Mælifell stands 791 meters above sea level, and it is a composite cone volcano formed by volcanic eruptions underneath the Myrdalsjökull glacier. Mælifell surfaced approximately 10,000 years ago as glaciers receded after the Last glacial period.
Apart from walking, Mount Mælifell is reachable only by a 4WD vehicle. It is on the southern Fjallabak road next to the glacier Mýrdalsjökull. The road is usually wet and sometimes completely flooded, making the volcano only accessible from July to the beginning of October.
